unique_issues.title: Incorrect historical chronology

evidence.quote: Early 1900s: These cards were first produced by tobacco companies.

unique_issues.reason: The chronology then jumps backward to 1871 and 1888; first-production framing conflicts with its own earlier dates.
unique_issues.recommended_action: Reorder chronologically and distinguish early tobacco issues from earlier baseball cards.
unique_issues.double_count_policy: Unique issue counted once; related diagnostic failures do not contribute additional penalties

unique_issues.title: Questionable graded-slab dimensions in table
unique_issues.reason: The chart lists 0.2 inch for the first slab dimension while the later PSA description says 3.2 inches; this is an internal contradiction.
unique_issues.recommended_action: Verify current slab manufacturer dimensions and correct the chart.
unique_issues.double_count_policy: Unique issue counted once; related diagnostic failures do not contribute additional penalties

unique_issues.title: Card-versus-slab dimensions insufficiently differentiated
unique_issues.reason: Grading case dimensions are mixed into a card-size chart without clearly identifying case width, height, and thickness.
unique_issues.recommended_action: Separate trading-card sizes from grading-holder exterior dimensions.
unique_issues.double_count_policy: Unique issue counted once; related diagnostic failures do not contribute additional penalties

unique_issues.title: Incorrect sleeve description

evidence.quote: Penny Sleeves: These boxes feature soft polypropylene sleeves.

unique_issues.reason: Penny sleeves are sleeves, not boxes.
unique_issues.recommended_action: Define penny sleeves as flexible plastic sleeves, and storage boxes separately.
unique_issues.double_count_policy: Unique issue counted once; related diagnostic failures do not contribute additional penalties

topic_search_intent.rationale: Provides direct size answer and usable conversion.

factual_technical_accuracy.rationale: Slab-size contradiction, historical chronology and authenticity overclaims.

semantic_information_value.rationale: Many card variants described, but categories and evidence need refinement.

practical_decision_support.rationale: Chart useful, production ordering details underdeveloped.

content_structure_readability.rationale: Clear sections but duplicated standard dimensions.

executive_summary.strengths: Clearly provides the standard 2.5 × 3.5-inch card size, accurate basic metric conversions and a 5:7 aspect ratio; comparison tables and sleeve/storage discussion support the topic.
executive_summary.critical_findings: Incorrect historical chronology; Questionable graded-slab dimensions in table; Card-versus-slab dimensions insufficiently differentiated; Incorrect sleeve description; Potentially misleading authenticity claim.
executive_summary.recommended_corrections: Reorder chronologically and distinguish early tobacco issues from earlier baseball cards.; Verify current slab manufacturer dimensions and correct the chart.; Separate trading-card sizes from grading-holder exterior dimensions.; Define penny sleeves as flexible plastic sleeves, and storage boxes separately.; State that size is one inspection factor and is not proof of authenticity..

source_verification.visual_exhibits: annotated published-text excerpts, NOT captured website screenshots

caveats: Wording, contradictions and structural issues were checked against published article text; some industry claims require authoritative vendor-specific validation.
